name: Saint Matthew the Apostle
history: A tax collector at Capernaum, despised as a collaborator with Rome, whom Jesus called from his booth with two words: follow me. He left everything, gave a feast for his old companions, and heard Christ say that He had come to call sinners. Tradition holds him to be the author of the first Gospel, written for Jewish Christians.
life: Mark and Luke call him Levi, son of Alphaeus; in the Gospel that bears his name he is Matthew the tax collector. Collecting customs by the Sea of Galilee, he would have been rich and unwelcome. When Jesus called him, he rose and followed, and soon invited Jesus to dine with tax collectors and sinners, which scandalised the Pharisees. Early writers, beginning with Papias, say that Matthew gathered the sayings of the Lord in the Hebrew language. His Gospel shows Jesus as the one in whom the Law and the Prophets are fulfilled, and gives us the visit of the Magi, the Sermon on the Mount, the Lord’s Prayer in the form we pray it and the command to make disciples of all nations. Traditions differ on where he preached and died, naming Ethiopia or Persia. His symbol is a winged man.
prayerTo: Saint Matthew, you left your counting table at a word from Christ and opened your house to sinners. Pray for all whose work is with money, that they may be honest and generous, and for me, that I may hear the Lord’s call today, rise without delay, and follow Him. Amen.
penance: Look honestly at your spending and give a generous share of something to the poor today, or settle a debt you have put off.
meditation: Jesus saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax office and said to him, follow me. What keeps you sitting at your table when Christ calls?
prayer: May we be helped, O Lord, by the prayers of the blessed Apostle and Evangelist Matthew, that what we ourselves cannot obtain, may be granted by his intercession. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
